arxiv-1710-00782.title: The Impact of Transceiver Noise on Digital Nonlinearity Compensation
arxiv-1710-00782.creator: Daniel Semrau, Domaniç Lavery, Lidia Galdino, Robert I. Killey, and Polina Bayvel
arxiv-1710-00782.description: Abstract The efficiency of digital nonlinearity compensation (NLC) is analyzed in the presence of noise arising from amplified spontaneous emission noise (ASE) as well as from a non-ideal transceiver subsystem. Its impact on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and reach increase is studied with particular emphasis on split NLC, where the digital back-propagation algorithm is divided between transmitter and receiver.

arxiv-2003-06562.title: Simultaneous Downlink Data Transmission and Uplink Channel Estimation with Reduced Complexity Full Duplex MIMO Radios
arxiv-2003-06562.creator: Md Atiqul Islam 2 , George C. Alexandropoulos 4 , and Besma Smida 2
arxiv-2003-06562.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Md Atiqul Islam 2 , George C. Alexandropoulos 4 , and Besma Smida 2. In this paper, we study Full Duplex (FD) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radios for simultaneous data communication and control information exchange. Capitalizing on a recently proposed FD MIMO architecture combining digital transmit and receive beamforming with reduced complexity multi-tap analog Self-Interference (SI) cancellation, we propose a novel transmission scheme exploiting channel reciprocity for joint downlink beamformed information data communication and uplink channel estimation through training data transmission.

arxiv-2107-07894.title: Relaxation-speed crossover in anharmonic potentials
arxiv-2107-07894.creator: Jan Meibohm, Danilo Forastiere, Tunrayo Adeleke-Larodo, Karel Proesmans
arxiv-2107-07894.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jan Meibohm, Danilo Forastiere, Tunrayo Adeleke-Larodo, Karel Proesmans. In a recent Letter [A. 125 , 110602 (2020)], thermal relaxation was observed to occur faster from cold to hot (heating) than from hot to cold (cooling). Here we show that overdamped diffusion in anharmonic potentials generically exhibits both faster heating and faster cooling, depending on the initial temperatures and on the potential’s degree of anharmonicity. We draw a relaxation-speed phase diagram that localises the different behaviours in parameter space.

arxiv-2403-01097.title: Mermaid Cereal: Interactions and Pattern Formation in a Macroscopic Magnetocapillary SALR System
arxiv-2403-01097.creator: Alireza Hooshanginejad, Jack-William Barotta, Victoria Spradlin, Giuseppe Pucci, Robert Hunt, Daniel M. Harris
arxiv-2403-01097.description: Abstract When particles are deposited at a fluid interface they tend to aggregate by capillary attraction to minimize the overall potential energy of the system. In this work, we embed floating millimetric disks with permanent magnets to introduce a competing repulsion effect and study their pattern formation in equilibrium.

arxiv-2502-05840.description: Abstract In the context of 2-player zero-sum infinite duration games played on (potentially infinite) graphs, the memory of an objective is the smallest integer k k such that in any game won by Eve, she has a strategy with ≤ k \leq k states of memory.

arxiv-2507-17051.title: Exact closure for discrete large-eddy simulation
arxiv-2507-17051.creator: Syver Døving Agdestein, Roel Verstappen, Benjamin Sanderse
arxiv-2507-17051.description: Abstract In this article we propose new discretization-consistent expressions for the sub-filter stress (SFS) tensor in discrete LES , where the filter is induced by the discretization. We introduce a new two-grid filter that allows us to exactly compute the SFS tensor when DNS data is available.

arxiv-2507-18458.title: Emergent-gravity Hall effect from quantum geometry
arxiv-2507-18458.creator: Hiroki Yoshida, Takehito Yokoyama
arxiv-2507-18458.description: Abstract We theoretically propose a Hall effect driven by effective gravitational fields arising from quantum geometry. We develop four mechanisms for this ”emergent-gravity Hall effect” : real-space gravity, momentum-space gravity, gravitional anomalous velocity, and gravitational Lorentz force which are described by the Christoffel symbols in real, momentum, and time spaces.

arxiv-2510-05764.title: RareAgent: Self-Evolving Reasoning for Drug Repurposing in Rare Diseases
arxiv-2510-05764.creator: Lang Qin, Zijian Gan, Xu Cao, Pengcheng Jiang, Yankai Jiang, Jiawei Han, Kaishun Wu, Jintai Chen
arxiv-2510-05764.description: Abstract Computational drug repurposing for rare diseases is especially challenging when no prior associations exist between drugs and target diseases. Therefore, knowledge graph completion and message-passing GNNs have little reliable signal to learn and propagate, resulting in poor performance. We present RareAgent, a self-evolving multi-agent system that reframes this task from passive pattern recognition to active evidence-seeking reasoning.

arxiv-2512-13196.title: Noise-Resilient Quantum Aggregation on NISQ for Federated ADAS Learning
arxiv-2512-13196.creator: Chethana K Sudarshan T S B
arxiv-2512-13196.description: Abstract Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) increasingly employ Federated Learning (FL) to collaboratively train models across distributed vehicular nodes while preserving data privacy. Yet, conventional FL aggregation remains susceptible to noise, latency, and security constraints inherent to real-time vehicular networks.

arxiv-2601-09372.title: Formally Verifying Noir Zero Knowledge Programs with NAVe
arxiv-2601-09372.creator: Pedro Antonino, Namrata Jain
arxiv-2601-09372.description: Abstract Zero-Knowledge (ZK) proof systems are cryptographic protocols that can (with overwhelming probability) demonstrate that the pair ( X , W ) (X,W) is in a relation R R without revealing information about the private input W W . This membership checking is captured by a complex arithmetic circuit: a set of polynomial equations over a finite field.

pmc-11621932.creator: Revathi Shanmugasundaram, Adeleye M. Ajao, Shahna Fathima, Adelumola Oladeinde, Ramesh K. Selvaraj, Todd J. Applegate, Oluyinka A. Olukosi
pmc-11621932.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The objective of this experiment was to study the effects of partial replacement of soybean meal (SBM) with canola meal (CM) or corn-distillers' dried grains with solubles (cDDGS) in reduced-protein (RP) diets for Eimeria-infected broilers. pmc-12563222.title: Role of Lipoprotein(a) and Blood Cells Ratios in Peripheral Artery Disease
pmc-12563222.creator: Alexandra V. Tyurina, Olga I. Afanasieva, Marat V. Ezhov, Narek A. Tmoyan, Tatiana V. Balakhonova, Sergei N. Pokrovsky
pmc-12563222.description: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a major global health issue. This study investigated the relationship between lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) to blood cells ratios, and PAD development. The study included 361 patients categorized into groups based on the presence of stenotic atherosclerosis in lower limb arteries (LLAs) diagnosed via duplex ultrasound.

pmc-12570257.title: Bridging the Gap in Carbon Free Iron Making: How Hydrogen Affects the Reduction of Iron Ore between 900 and 1590 °C
pmc-12570257.creator: Ram Krushna Mohanta, Dallin Fisher, Yuri Korobeinikov, Qijun Hong, Christopher Muhich, Seetharaman Sridhar, Noemi Leick
pmc-12570257.description: Hydrogen-based reduction of iron ore for iron and steel production has emerged as a promising alternative to coal and natural gas. Unlike other hydrogen-based iron ore reduction studies, this research focuses on a wide temperature range across 900–1590 °C, encompassing reduction in solid, mixed, and liquid (slag) phases.
